## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Kusalattika, Vedanāttika* (Patthana 17.1) is a text within the Paṭṭhāna of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It comprises the first combination of triads (*tika*), pairing the Wholesome Triad (*kusalattika*) with the Feeling Triad (*vedanāttika*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its exposition treats conditional dependencies; in its opening chapter on being dependent (*paṭicca-vāra*), it analyzes formulations such as how, dependent on a wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling, a corresponding phenomenon associated with pleasant feeling arises conditioned by way of root [Nyanatiloka 2007].

Text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus indicate that the work shares 1,558 matching passages with 113 other Pali texts, reflecting the standardized repetitive formulas characteristic of the Paṭṭhāna [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments occur with related triad and dyad permutations in the Paṭṭhāna, including *Kusalattika, Tika* (Patthana 5.1), *Kusalattika, Vedanāttika* (Patthana 11.1, Patthana 23.1), *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1), and the inverted pairing *Vedanāttika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 11.10) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus aligns passages in the text with the Sanskrit Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma work *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus].
